subtopics.title: Three Ways to Measure One Economy

questions.question: Why must the production, expenditure and income methods arrive at the same total?
options: Whatever is produced is sold, whatever is sold is paid for, and every rand paid becomes income in somebody's hands
The three methods all use the same survey forms
The law requires the totals to be published as equal
Each method counts intermediate goods at full value

questions.question: Sugar delivered to a cold-drink bottler and sugar in a family's shopping trolley are classified differently because:
options: Bottlers buy sugar at a wholesale discount
Classification follows the buyer's PURPOSE, not the product — the bottler's sugar is intermediate, the family's is final
Sugar sold to firms is exempt from VAT
Household sugar is a durable good

questions.question: A GROSS aggregate becomes a NET aggregate once you remove:
options: Imports
Taxes on products
Consumption of fixed capital — the year's wearing-out of machines, vehicles and buildings
Government transfer payments

questions.question: The correct statement of the DOMESTIC versus NATIONAL distinction is:
options: Domestic totals exclude government activity; national totals include it
Domestic is measured at basic prices; national at market prices
The two words are interchangeable in the national accounts
Domestic asks WHERE production happened — inside the borders; national asks WHO earns the income — residents, wherever their assets sit

questions.question: The four classes of household consumption spending are:
options: Durable goods, semi-durable goods, non-durable goods and services
Necessities, luxuries, imports and exports
Cash, credit, debit and lay-by purchases
Food, transport, housing and entertainment

questions.question: When household incomes tighten, spending on durables falls first because:
options: Durables carry the highest VAT rate
Durable purchases can be DELAYED, while non-durables like maize meal cannot
Shops withdraw credit on durables in a downturn
Durables are mostly imported

questions.question: A social grant is excluded from G because:
options: Grants are financed by borrowing, not taxes
Grants are paid monthly rather than annually
It is a TRANSFER — government receives no good or service in return, and the rand is counted once inside C when the household spends it
Grants are recorded as government investment

questions.question: Government builds a new water treatment works. In the national accounts this is recorded under:
options: G, since government financed it
C, since households will drink the water
The change in inventories
I — gross fixed capital formation — because an asset was created, not consumed

questions.question: Gross fixed capital formation is defined as spending on:
options: Assets that serve in production repeatedly for longer than a year — buildings, construction works, machinery, vehicles, ICT and cultivated biological assets
Everything a firm buys during the year
Financial assets such as shares and government bonds
Raw materials waiting in the storeroom

questions.question: A firm buys an existing office block from another firm. This is NOT capital formation because:
options: Office blocks are not fixed assets
The nation's stock of assets is unchanged — the building merely changed owners
The purchase was financed with a loan
Property transactions are recorded in C

questions.question: Gross fixed capital formation is R1 000 billion and consumption of fixed capital is R620 billion. Net investment is:
options: R1 620 billion
R620 billion
R380 billion
R1 000 billion

questions.question: Investment of R1 000 billion against GDP of R6 700 billion is about 14,9 per cent. Measured against the National Development Plan's investment goal, this is:
options: Slightly above the goal
Exactly in line with the goal
Irrelevant, because the plan sets no investment goal
Less than half of the roughly 30 per cent of GDP the plan calls for

subtopics.title: GVA, GNE and GNI — the Chain of Conversions

questions.question: C is 4 200, G is 1 500, I is 1 000 and inventories FELL by 60, all in rand billions. GNE is:
options: R6 640 billion
R6 760 billion
R6 700 billion
R5 700 billion

questions.question: With GNE of 6 640, exports of 2 100 and imports of 2 040, GDP at market prices is:
options: R6 580 billion
R6 700 billion
R8 740 billion
R6 640 billion

questions.question: GVA at basic prices is converted into GDP at market prices by:
options: Adding exports and subtracting imports
Adding consumption of fixed capital
Adding taxes on products and subtracting subsidies on products
Subtracting net primary income paid abroad

questions.question: GDP is 6 700; primary income received from abroad is 110 and primary income paid abroad is 290. GNI is:
options: R6 880 billion
R6 990 billion
R6 700 billion
R6 520 billion — below GDP because more primary income flows out of South Africa than flows in

questions.question: On the country's year-long till slip, the towering pile is:
options: C — household spending, roughly sixty cents of every rand on the slip
G — the state's day-to-day shopping
I — the building-things pile
Imports

questions.question: A taxi ride belongs to which class of household spending?
options: Non-durable goods
Services — once you climb out, there is nothing to show for it but having arrived
Semi-durable goods
Durable goods

questions.question: Gogo's pension grant does not sit on the government pile because:
options: Pensions are counted as savings
The grant is smaller than a government salary
Government bought nothing when it paid her — the spending is counted once, in C, when she buys bread and tea
Grants are exempt from VAT

questions.question: Appliance showrooms go quiet months before food shops in a downturn because:
options: Appliances rise in price faster than food
Food shops advertise more heavily
Appliance shops depend on imports
The washing machine can be postponed and the oranges cannot — durables fall first, non-durables hold

questions.question: A bakery buys R150 000 of flour, R60 000 of packaging and a R500 000 industrial oven. The capital item is:
options: The oven — it will still be baking in ten years, while the flour and packaging are used up
The flour
The packaging
All three, since a business bought them

questions.question: A macadamia orchard counts as fixed capital because:
options: Nuts are classified as durable goods
The tree yields output year after year — a slow machine that manufactures nuts for thirty years
Orchards appreciate in market value
Farm produce is exported

questions.question: The bakery spends R500 000 on a new oven while its old oven suffers R180 000 of wear. The true gain in baking capacity is:
The investment pile is the special one among the spending piles because:
options: It is the largest pile on the till slip
It is the only pile taxed at a lower rate
It is funded entirely by government
It is the only spending that makes NEXT year's output bigger — the production possibility curve shifting outward

questions.question: In plain words, GNE is:
options: The whole till slip added up — what the people of this country SPENT
What producers received before taxes on products
What residents keep after paying foreign owners
The value of goods sold abroad

questions.question: GNE is 6 640 while GDP is 6 700, with exports of 2 100 and imports of 2 040. This tells you that:
options: The national accounts contain an error of 60
Production beat residents' spending by 60 billion, and the surplus left the country as net exports
Imports exceeded exports this year
Inventories must have risen by 60

questions.question: GVA of 6 000 becomes GDP of 6 700 once you:
options: Add net primary income from the rest of the world
Subtract consumption of fixed capital
Add R730 billion of taxes on products and subtract R30 billion of subsidies
Add the change in inventories

questions.question: South Africans keep R6 520 billion of the R6 700 billion produced because:
options: R180 billion was lost to depreciation
R180 billion was collected as VAT
R180 billion of stock stayed unsold on shelves
Net primary income of R180 billion flowed out — profit and interest earned here but owed to foreign owners
